headline: Wayfinding is how we mentally map and navigate spaces—a skill that shrinks with disuse
universal_truth: Skills atrophy without practice; convenience can cost capability
fun_facts: London taxi drivers have measurably larger hippocampi—the brain's navigation center—from memorizing 25,000 streets
Studies show GPS use may shrink the hippocampus and reduce spatial memory
Animals that navigate long distances—like migrating birds—have specialized brain regions humans lack
discussion_questions: Has GPS changed your ability to find your way?
What skills have you lost because technology handles them?
How do you balance convenience with capability?

hook.script: London taxi drivers spend years memorizing 25,000 streets—and their brains physically grow larger in the hippocampus, the navigation center. Meanwhile, studies suggest GPS users may be losing spatial memory. Navigation is a skill that grows or shrinks with use.

cliff.script: GPS gives us perfect navigation—but at what cost? If we outsource navigation to technology, what happens to our own wayfinding ability?
cliff.prompt: What happens when we stop navigating ourselves?

options.text: The brain regions for spatial memory may weaken, reducing our ability to navigate without help
options.response: Yes. Use it or lose it. Brain regions that go unused don't maintain themselves. Convenience has cognitive costs.

options.text: Nothing changes—we just use a tool like we use calculators for math
options.response: Tools do extend ability, but spatial memory is connected to overall cognitive health...

fact1.title: The Taxi Driver Brain
fact1.script: London's famous 'Knowledge' test requires taxi drivers to memorize thousands of routes. Brain scans show their hippocampi—the memory-and-navigation regions—are significantly larger than average. Navigation literally grows the brain.

fact2.title: GPS Trade-off
fact2.script: Research suggests heavy GPS reliance correlates with reduced hippocampal activity and worse spatial memory. We navigate successfully but build no mental map. The destination is reached; the capability is lost.

fact3.title: Cognitive Reserve
fact3.script: Spatial navigation engages brain regions linked to memory and cognitive health. Some researchers believe active navigation may build 'cognitive reserve'—protection against age-related mental decline. Navigation might be brain exercise.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Skills atrophy without practice. Navigation teaches that convenience can cost capability. Choose deliberately what to outsource—the skills you don't use are the skills you lose.

outro.script: That's Day 108. Tomorrow, we'll explore how we track time. Until then, navigate somewhere without GPS—give your hippocampus a workout.

growTrack.title: Wayfinding Exercise - Build Your Mental Map
growTrack.activity: Navigate somewhere familiar without GPS today. Pay attention to landmarks, turns, and distances. Try to build a mental map as you go. Afterward, could you give directions? Regular practice keeps this skill sharp.
